review_type: targeted primary-source literature review, not systematic review
scope: Research-agent benchmark design for public PCNSL imaging-genomic analysis; no new model experiments in this review
verification_note: Claims are limited to the source portions described per entry. Most benchmark scope claims were verified in primary abstracts; no claim of full-text review for all papers. Publication years use first preprint year unless journal publication is explicitly intended. Design recommendations are author proposals rather than reported source findings.

sources.title: InfiAgent-DABench: Evaluating Agents on Data Analysis Tasks
sources.contribution: Closed-form analysis answers; 257 questions from 52 CSV files.
sources.limitations: Task success does not by itself establish scientific validity.

sources.title: DSBench: How Far Are Data Science Agents from Becoming Data Science Experts?
sources.contribution: 466 analysis and 74 modeling tasks.
sources.limitations: Older evaluated models and task definitions cannot establish current frontier difficulty.

sources.title: MLAgentBench: Evaluating Language Agents on Machine Learning Experimentation
sources.contribution: 13 experimentation tasks with tools and executable artifacts.
sources.limitations: Familiarity and public-task contamination remain concerns.

sources.title: ScienceAgentBench: Toward Rigorous Assessment of Language Agents for Data-Driven Scientific Discovery
sources.contribution: 102 tasks from 44 papers, four disciplines, nine experts; ICLR 2025.
sources.limitations: Python artifact success is not universal evidence of clinical applicability.

sources.title: MLGym: A New Framework and Benchmark for Advancing AI Research Agents
sources.contribution: 13 open-ended research tasks; iterative experimentation environments.
sources.limitations: Improved optimization is distinct from scientifically justified inference.

sources.title: RE-Bench: Evaluating frontier AI R&D capabilities of language model agents against human experts
sources.contribution: Seven environments and 71 eight-hour attempts by 61 human experts; time budget changes comparisons.
sources.limitations: The official report PDF exceeded the web tool size limit; claims here use the abstract, not a claimed full PDF review.

sources.title: MLE-bench: Evaluating Machine Learning Agents on Machine Learning Engineering
sources.contribution: 75 Kaggle competitions; engineering metrics and human leaderboard comparison.
sources.limitations: Predictive score is not a scientific-validity rubric.

sources.title: BLADE: Benchmarking Language Model Agents for Data-Driven Science
sources.contribution: 12 datasets/questions and expert analytical decisions; multiple valid analyses.
sources.limitations: Strong novelty overlap with open-ended scientific analysis; do not claim first.

sources.title: PaperBench: Evaluating AI’s Ability to Replicate AI Research
sources.contribution: 20 papers; 8,316 author-informed grading tasks; separate judge evaluation.
sources.limitations: Automated judging must itself be validated.

sources.title: AI-Researcher: Autonomous Scientific Innovation
sources.contribution: Introduces Scientist-Bench with guided innovation and open exploration.
sources.limitations: Author-reported paper quality does not establish reproducible clinical validity.

sources.title: AstaBench
sources.contribution: Scientific-agent suite with shared tools and explicit tool-access distinctions.
sources.limitations: Dynamic project; this review does not reproduce leaderboard measurements.

sources.title: ReplicatorBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Replicability in Social and Behavioral Sciences
sources.contribution: Human-verified replicable and non-replicable claims; extraction, execution, interpretation; KDD 2026 AI4Sciences.
sources.limitations: New-data replication differs from computational reproduction.

sources.title: SciIntegrity-Bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Academic Integrity in AI Scientist Systems
sources.contribution: 33 scenarios in 11 trap categories; honest failure versus completion pressure.
sources.limitations: Preprint; integrity categories are study definitions, not proof of intentional deception.

sources.title: PAPERBENCHX: Can AI Reproduce Science Across Disciplines?
sources.contribution: 93 expert-created tasks in 12 research areas; scoring regenerated evidence after replay.
sources.limitations: October 2026 preprint; numerical results are not reproduced here.

sources.title: RealDataAgentBench
sources.contribution: Software benchmark with documented lexical-validity grading limitations and calibration discussion.
sources.limitations: Not treated as a peer-reviewed study or reliable gold-standard judge.

sources.title: PROBAST+AI: an updated quality, risk of bias, and applicability assessment tool for prediction models using regression or artificial intelligence methods
sources.contribution: Distinguishes development quality, evaluation bias, and applicability.
sources.limitations: Imprecision is not synonymous with bias; not a prescription for one algorithm.

sources.title: TRIPOD+AI statement: updated guidance for reporting clinical prediction models that use regression or machine learning methods
sources.contribution: Transparent reporting for prediction-model development and evaluation.
sources.limitations: Reporting completeness alone cannot establish methodological validity.

sources.title: Checklist for Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging (CLAIM): 2024 Update
sources.contribution: Imaging provenance, reference-standard terminology, internal and external testing.
sources.limitations: A supplied annotation is a reference standard, not absolute anatomical truth.

sources.title: Leakage and the Reproducibility Crisis in ML-based Science
sources.contribution: Leakage taxonomy and consequences for scientific reproducibility.
sources.limitations: Use mechanism-specific tests; a checklist word is not behavioral evidence.

sources.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
sources.contribution: Model selection can overfit a noisy evaluation criterion.
sources.limitations: Selection strategy and estimand determine appropriate evaluation design.

sources.title: Cross-validation failure: Small sample sizes lead to large error bars
sources.contribution: Small-sample cross-validation uncertainty; fold variability can misrepresent uncertainty.
sources.limitations: Repeated folds do not create independent clinical subjects.

sources.title: Recent Frontier Models Are Reward Hacking
sources.contribution: Observed evaluation gaming motivates trace inspection and grader isolation.
sources.limitations: Do not infer intention or broad prevalence from an individual scientific error.
